prompt.en: A receiver stage takes a 7 MHz modulated signal and produces a larger voltage at the same frequency with the same modulation. Which block behaviour fits?

feedback.en: The stage raises the existing RF level while preserving frequency and information.
Detection recovers the information as audio. The described output is still modulated RF at 7 MHz.
A frequency-converting mixer moves the signal to another frequency. The described carrier frequency did not change.
An oscillator generates a repeating signal. Here an existing input is being made larger with its modulation preserved.

explanation.en: Gain can apply to RF or audio. Identify the signal type and whether frequency or information changed, not just whether the output grew.

prompt.en: An audio amplifier is overdriven until voice peaks flatten. Which interpretation fits the change in waveform shape?

text.en: Uniform gain reduction that preserves the full speech waveform.

feedback.en: Uniform scaling preserves shape. Flattening only the peaks changes the relative shape of the waveform.

text.en: Non-linear clipping that can create extra frequency products.

feedback.en: The output no longer follows the input proportionally. Clipping changes the shape and can create unwanted products.

text.en: Linear gain with greater output headroom for the same voice peaks.

feedback.en: Headroom is room for peaks before clipping. Flattened peaks show that the clean range has been exceeded.

text.en: Filtering that removes only background noise while retaining the original peaks.

feedback.en: The wanted speech peaks themselves changed. This is not evidence that only unwanted noise was removed.

explanation.en: Linearity concerns preserving shape, not simply making the output louder or more efficient. Excess drive can turn useful gain into distortion.

prompt.en: A training supply has a sine-wave input and output pulses of the same polarity on both half-cycles, even with its smoothing capacitor removed. Which function produced that change?

text.en: Holding output near a fixed voltage with a regulator.

feedback.en: Regulation holds voltage closer to a target as conditions change. It is not what steers both AC half-cycles into the same polarity.

text.en: Storing charge between peaks with a filter capacitor.

feedback.en: The pulses remain when the capacitor is removed. Filtering smooths pulses rather than creating the one-polarity waveform.

text.en: Steering current with a bridge rectifier.

feedback.en: The bridge uses diode direction to make both half-cycles feed the same DC polarity. Filtering is a later job.

text.en: Blocking a reversed battery with a series protection diode.

feedback.en: A series input diode can block a reversed DC source. It does not steer both halves of AC into a full-wave output.

explanation.en: Rectification changes current direction behaviour. Filtering smooths the result, while regulation controls the output level.
